tagline: Down the island under the live oaks, to the beach.
intro: From the Dawhoo River bridge, SC 174 runs the length of Edisto Island to the Atlantic, across salt marsh and creeks and through maritime forest and farm fields. It travels under old live oaks, past small homes, prayer chapels, churches and country stores, and at roadside stands the baskets are sweetgrass.

The island grew long-staple Sea Island cotton on the labor of enslaved Africans, who developed the Gullah language and culture of the islands and the Lowcountry. In the 1920s the way onto it was across the marsh at low tide, on beds of oyster shell. The beach is still where the road gives out.

moments.title: Edisto Island Presbyterian Church
moments.text: A congregation gathered in 1685 worships in a church built in 1831, with its burying ground alongside.

moments.title: Botany Bay
moments.text: Two old plantations made into one state preserve, where three 1840s outbuildings of Bleak Hall survive. Its Sea Island cotton once sold to lace-makers in Belgium and France.

moments.title: Edisto Beach State Park
moments.text: Trails through the maritime forest lead to a Native American shell midden dated to 2000 BC, in a park the Civilian Conservation Corps built on land given in 1935.
